summary: Sharpened the one part of the audit still carried as a loose derivation and closed the last named variant as far as source allows. The parent account said peers receiving a forwarded compaction recompute the bound against their own decided index and, with the same drifted decided index, are read to mirror the leader's loss; that sentence is true as conditioned but left the other branch implicit. Reading the peer-side handler shows it: handle_compaction applies the forwarded compaction through the node's own trim or snapshot path and discards the result (mod.rs 217-227, whose comment states that errors are ignored because the data will still be kept), while the snapshot path refuses an index above the receiver's own decided index with UndecidedIndex and the trim path refuses one above its own minimum recorded accepted index. So a peer compacts to the leader's index only when its own decided index already covers it - and then builds its own snapshot from its own storage range, which for the compacting node in the observed receipt was empty - and a peer whose decided index lies below the forwarded index quietly keeps its state where it was, the opposite of mirroring the loss. That two-branch behaviour, with the handler material added in the same update and the reason no execution samples it (every compaction in this run was local_only or leader-side), is now recorded as a knowledge entry, so the audit's last derived item is derived explicitly rather than asserted loosely. No other record changed, nothing was executed, and no gaps remain registered: every question in the run carries a current account with its own receipts, controls, counterevidence and limits.
